  central object's offset `-sum(M_i rel_i) / M_total` and every member's
  position, derived and cached, marked stale up the parent chain when a
  member is added, removed or changes parent (the state is then
  re-expressed about the new parent so no position jumps) or its mass
  changes; it generalises `physics/system_tree.member_offsets_au` to a
  central child plus n members (n = 1 is today's binary formula, bit for
  bit); `valid_system(host)` checks every member is at most the
  mass-ratio limit of the central object or is a binary node. Sums are
  formed from relative numbers only (a double at 8 kpc has a spacing of
  32,768 m). Done: the invariants of TEST.242 pass.
  Prerequisites: GEN.565, GEN.315. Related: GEN.550, GEN.552, GEN.315,
  GEN.565.

  the central object is the heaviest member by the total mass of each
  branch (a sub-system counts as the sum of its parts; a tie under 1e-9
  relative keeps the draw order); the same sum gives the central
  object's velocity `-sum(M_i v_rel_i) / M_total` and a body's velocity
  in any ancestor's frame is the sum of the hops, leaf first, each hop
  advanced from its own epoch (analytic two-body orbit with mu = G
  (M_central + M_member); the outer system's tide is a stability gate,
  not a force). The step that makes the heaviest primary is GEN.581.

  barycentre are unchanged) and every absolute position is identical.

  need it. Done: a pair re-primaried gives identical absolute positions,
  the step from the originals is idempotent and independent of listing
  order, and no second copy of the swap is left.

  disruption for the core ring; the fill ships as the labelled stand-in
  meanwhile. A change to the stored clusters rides the pending epoch and
  the one wiped rescatter. Done: the note names the sources with their
  evidence state, gives the upper mass and the disruption law with their
  scatter, and a test shows the young clusters of the core above 5e3

- [ ] **GEN.633 The backfill after a run puts its dimmer bright stars only in sectors not yet generated, so a sector holds different systems depending on the order the sectors were generated in (bug)**
  Found by Core 1 (relayed 3:07 AM EDT 2026-10-23 as the lane reported)
  while building TEST.181. Kind: order dependence. Fails on main: yes,
  every time (not a flake). Reproducer: plan a wide toy galaxy
  (tests.test_galaxy_gen._plan_wide_galaxy with seed
  0123456789ABCDEF0011223344556677), then run `planetgen galaxy --shells
  S --bands B --wedges W --num-systems 4 --workers 1` once per sector
  (default `--backfill-from edge`) for (1,0,0), (1,0,5), (1,0,11),
  (1,1,0) in that order, and again in the reverse order. Result: sector
  (1,0,0) holds 4 systems when generated first and 8 when generated
  last, (1,0,5) holds 6 and 11, (1,1,0) holds 6 and 4, and (1,0,11) is
  the same in both orders. Cause: the backfill after a run places the
  dimmer bright stars only in cells that are not yet generated, so a
  sector generated before the backfill reaches its cell never gets those
  stars, while a sector the backfill reached first is built around them
  (4 bright stars plus the 4 requested). So GEN.57's sentence that a
  sector's contents come out the same whichever sectors were generated
  before it still fails for the backfill, and GEN.306, GEN.307 and
  TEST.181 do not close it. This is a design question and TEST.181 does
  not decide it. Candidates (Core 1's): (a) fill an already-generated
  sector with the stars when the backfill reaches it; (b) make the first
  fill take the deeper floor, so no later pass adds stars. Boss decides
  whether it is needed before 8.1 (the TODO thread put a card to him); it is a prerequisite
  of GEN.57 and so of TEST.77.
  Decided (Boss, card tap, 8:29 AM EDT 2026-10-23, option A "Yes, before
  8.1; first fill goes deeper"): candidate (b). The first fill takes the
  deeper floor, so no later pass adds stars to a sector. Do: build (b)
  with a test that the four sectors above hold the same systems in both
  orders. Done: that test passes and TEST.181 gains the backfill case.
  Owner: Core 1 (it found the bug, owns GEN.57 and GEN.55, and the item is
  in 8.1; 8.1 queue, Boss's card answer 8:29 AM EDT 2026-10-23).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: GEN.57, GEN.44, GEN.42, GEN.309,
  TEST.181.
  Design: [docs/design/generation/reproducible-galaxies.md](design/generation/reproducible-galaxies.md)

- [ ] **GEN.648 The generation request for a habitable world (+habitable_world) runs an ordered ladder of nine adaptations before it gives up: redraw the surface, restrict the planet, more starting water, aquifers, regenerate the planet, adapt the system, add a brighter primary, regenerate the star, then the best result**
  Decided (Boss, 6:09 PM EDT 2026-10-23, card option 3 of GEN.644, 'A
  then D', relayed by the coordinator): 'Let's go with 3, since we're
  doing compositions, let's leave out the class designation until planet
  generation is completed, then fill in the classes based on the
  atmosphere (even no atmosphere) composition / pressure, average
  surface temperature, terrestrial composition (i.e. a rocky planet
  composition), gas composition (for gas giants), same for moons. The
  reason I did classes the way they are now is because I didn't know how
  to get the compositions correct.' Proposal and options:
  /mnt/project-files/reports/phi6-and-planet-classes-proposal-2026-10-23.md
  (options A, B, C are retired). Part of GEN.644 (design) and GEN.643
  (the habitable rule). Owner: Habitability lane D unless stated.
  Replace the class-list steering (LIFE_PLANET_CLASSES). Boss (7:12 PM
  EDT 2026-10-23, answering through lane D): a habitable-world request
  runs an ordered ladder of adaptations before it quits. After each
  attempt the failing domain of the finished score (Water, Temperature,
  Radiation, Suitability) and the star's history loss pick the next step.
  The aim is a PHI-6 overall of Blue or Green; the accepted end is Yellow
  with Suitability at least Yellow (Boss, 6:54 PM EDT). The ladder:
  (1) redraw the surface (albedo, greenhouse, atmosphere, life draws of
  the same planet); (2) restrict the planet parameters (mass 0.5 to 2
  Earth masses, rocky, low eccentricity, usable rotation and tilt);
  (3) more starting water, an Ocean World (initial water = the history
  loss / mass plus an Earth-like remainder; the class follows the
  finished composition under GEN.644 option 3); (4) aquifers (the
  aquifer item of this list, which also covers the Yellow fallback);
  (5) regenerate the planet in the same slot (whole new body from a
  derived sub-seed, never an edit); (6) adapt the system (6a place the
  zone planet in the outer part of the zone, 6b move or remove a giant
  that blocks the slot); (7) add a brighter, heavier primary (Boss, 7:23
  PM EDT, correcting the earlier companion idea): the failing red dwarf
  system is kept unchanged (stars, planets, moons, belts, ids) and
  becomes the secondary of a WIDE binary; the new primary gets its own
  planets and the habitable steps run on its zone; repeat once for a
  third star; wide-binary stability (separation floor from both systems'
  reach, S-type limit, triple rule) is part of the step; the main new
  code is a member-tree mode that adds a primary above an existing
  system, plus designation changes (A becomes B); (8) regenerate the star
  (the last resort; a failing M dwarf is redrawn up to N times; a failing
  G or K star keeps its star and goes to step 9 unless Boss wants those
  redrawn); (9) give up with the best result found, Yellow if Suitability
  allows, recorded as unmet or fallback, never silently. Each step has an attempt cap and a seed per
  (step, attempt); suggested caps K1 8, K2 6, K3 6, K4 1, K5 6, K6 4
  each, K7 4 per added primary, K8 8 stars (design values), and a budget of attempts per request
  so a directed sector cannot run for ever. The outcome records the step
  reached and how many star draws it took. Design:
  /mnt/project-files/design-drafts/red-dwarf-water-and-star-regeneration-2026-10-23.md
  (section a, the honest note on 6c: a companion cannot make the host
  heavier or brighter, so it helps little for lost water). Done: a
  forced request is met by a Blue or Green world, or by the stated
  fallback, in every one of 120 forced systems that has an ecosphere (the
  proposal measured 7 of 120 before), the step reached is counted per
  request, the draws are deterministic across worker counts, and a
  request that cannot be met names the failing domain and the step.
  Decided (Boss, 6:39 PM EDT 2026-10-23, relayed by the coordinator):
  'there is no recalculation never redraws composition rule, at least I
  don't remember one' (bulk-composition.md decision 31 / F10 was a lane

  Green first; the Yellow fallback is taken only after the stated cap on

- [ ] **GEN.709 Stored close-pair star positions disagree with the orbit_nodes tree after the multi-star work: a circular pair keeps a random arg_periapsis, and deeper trees are far off (bug)**
  Found by Lane 4 while stress-running TEST.130
  (test_the_scene_positions_at_the_epoch_match_the_stored_ones) on main,
  as the lane reported at 6:57 AM EDT 2026-10-24; report
  /mnt/project-files/reports/lane4/test-130-finding-2026-10-24.md with a
  replay script in
  /mnt/project-files/reports/lane4/test130-scan-repro.py. The test fails
  2 runs in 15 at the star assertion because it picks a multi-star
  system at random. Cause: for a circular close pair the stored phase
  (binary_secondary_position_* from the pair's phase_deg) is measured
  from the ascending node, but the orbit_nodes row holds
  mean_anomaly_deg = phase AND a random non-zero arg_periapsis_deg, so
  the tree places the star at omega plus phase (seed 1: 2.965 degrees
  off, exactly that angle). In deeper trees the pair-position columns
  and the tree disagree far more (seed 8, 5 stars: about 90 times
  different for the star the scene calls around barycenter). Do: make
  the node's omega and mean anomaly agree with the stored phase (a
  circular orbit takes omega 0, or the stored position is taken from the
  tree), in db/orbit_trees.py star_places and the multistar node build,
  and one source for the position. Done: the scene positions at the
  epoch equal the stored positions for every star of a seeded sample
  that includes pairs and trees of 3 or more stars, and TEST.130 passes
  50 runs in a row. This may change generator output, so it takes the
  next free generator epoch. Owner: Core 3 (it owns GEN.630 and GEN.631;
  proposed).
  Research (2026-10-09, Update): Core 3 accepted this (6:58 AM EDT
  2026-10-24, as the lane reported): it takes GEN.709 right after
  GEN.332 slice 1 merges and takes the next free generator epoch at
  merge.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: TEST.130, GEN.630, GEN.631.

- [ ] **GEN.710 A pre-placed row with a stored tree can have a member heavier than the row star at stars[0], so the nebula it lights and the star page disagree with the built sector (bug)**
  Found by Bug Hunt while fixing TEST.311 (#2945), as the lane reported
  at 7:22 AM EDT 2026-10-24. Pre-placed rows with stored trees
  (scatter_companions.star_tree) use the same multistar.draw_member_tree
  as the fill. A member can then be heavier than the row star, so the
  built system has it at stars[0]. run_sector.add_star_hosted_nebulae
  lights the nebula from stars[0], while the GEN.530 row prediction
  (row_nebula) uses the row star, so the star page and the uncharted
  scene can disagree with the built sector. Evidence: a drawn tree for
  one O7V row gave members O7V 18.74, B2V 10.4, B5V 6.93 solar masses in
  a k=30 case on old main; the mismatch appears whenever a companion
  out-masses the primary. Do: either light the nebula from the row star,
  or order the members so the row star stays first (the choice may
  change generated output and then needs the next free generator epoch,
  now 77). Done: for a sample of rows with trees, the nebula built in
  the sector equals the row_nebula prediction, with a test that forces a
  companion heavier than the primary. Owner: Core 3 (it owns the member
  tree; proposed).
  Research (2026-10-09, Update): Core 3 accepted this (7:23 AM EDT
  2026-10-24, as the lane reported): order is GEN.332 slice 1, then
  GEN.709, GEN.710, then the rest of GEN.332 and GEN.640; it takes the
  next free epoch at each merge.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: GEN.530, GEN.631, GEN.709, TEST.311.

- [ ] **PERF.111 `ResponseCache.put` without a database never trims the page cache: the cache grows past `max_entries`, and the thread test fails when its last put is one of those (bug)**
  Found by Core 2 (2026-10-17, 6:31 AM EDT as the lane reported, MAP.217
  gate unit phase), filed by the TODO thread, who read the code.
  `src/planetgen/web/lib/pagecache.py` `ResponseCache.put`: the `db is
  None` branch stores the entry and returns without the `while
  len(self._entries) > self._max_entries: popitem()` that the keyed
  branch (and `_recall`) have, so entries of the no-database kind are
  never evicted. Test:
  `src/tests/test_caches_threads.py::test_page_cache_fills_reads_and_clears_from_many_threads`
  failed with `assert 51 <= 50`. Fails on main: yes (deterministic).
  Frequency: 1 of 1 in the MAP.217 gate unit phase (1 failed, 18,311
  passed, 3,793 s); it passes alone 3 of 3 because it fails only when
  the last put of the run is a db=None one. Reproducer, no threads:
  `cache = pagecache.ResponseCache(lambda db, since: {"stamp": "s",
  "state": None}, dict(pagecache.DEFAULTS, max_entries=3,
  stamp_seconds=0))`, then 6 times `cache.put(None, f"/x/{n}", "body",
  cache.begin(None))`: `len(cache)` is 6, should be 3. Do: the same trim
  loop in the db-None branch (inside the lock, after the store), and a
  deterministic test of the reproducer above next to the thread test.
  Done: the reproducer gives 3, the thread test passes whatever the last
  put is, and a test asserts the bound for db=None puts alone. Owner:
  Core 2 (proposed; it offered to carry the three lines in its next PR,
  which is the cheapest route).
  Checked by the TODO thread (2026-10-17, 6:28 AM EDT, main with #2004):
  the reproducer above gives len(cache) 6 with max_entries 3, so the
  finding stands.
  Owner: Bug Hunt (bugs only, Boss, 2026-10-17, 10:06 AM EDT). This
  replaces any earlier owner line on this item.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: PERF.104, TEST.54.

- [ ] **PERF.119 The Generate page, the API and the one-off sector and system commands start their runs through the wrapper**
  Boss, 2026-10-17, 4:12 PM EDT: "Rework so every part of the generate
  process, all the scatter phases, are individual commands, then a
  general process wrapper makes a list of the commands that need to be
  run, and then puts those into the redis queue individually." The
  wrapper builds the command list, each command is one queue item. Once
  the stages are commands (PERF.106 to PERF.108), every way to start
  generation uses the one wrapper of PERF.118: the Generate page
  (`web/generate_page.py`, `web/job_runner.py`), the API jobs
  (`queue/api_jobs.py`) and the one-off `planetgen sector` and
  `planetgen system` commands (each a one-command run), so there is no
  second way to run a stage and no start path that skips the run record.
  Done: each of those entry points builds its command list with the
  wrapper and queues it; a test starts a run from each and finds it on
  the run record; a grep finds no stage started outside the wrapper.
  Owner: Core 5 (after PERF.98, before PERF.99 reads the run record on
  the pages).
  Decided (Boss, 2026-10-17, 4:15 PM EDT): from the command line Boss
  runs `plan`, then `scatter`; each scatter kind is its own command even
  where the root command is the same (a scatter command for only mass,
  only luminosity, only phenomena, only the nebula field, only the
  backfill, and so on, never one command that groups them). Each command
  has its own parameters, which the UX sets when it runs the commands
  through the API and which Boss sets on the command line. When a new
  generate job is called, the wrapper ONLY selects the commands that
  will run and never touches the others; they run in sequence; the
  progress bars are dynamic to the current context and show only what is
  going to run (the overall bar, the stage count and the estimate come
  from the selected commands alone). So each entry point sends its own
  parameters per command, and its progress shows only the commands
  selected.
  Decided (Boss, 2026-10-17, 4:18 PM EDT): the governing principle of
  PERF.118 holds for every start path: each entry point only builds the
  list of steps from what the user requested and hands it to the
  wrapper, which alone handles the sequence.
  The command inventory (docs/design/architecture/command-inventory.md, PERF.120)
  lists every other command and entry point.
  Decided (Boss, 2026-10-18, 5:14 to 5:15 PM EDT, cards F1 to F4, all as
  Core 5 recommended, relayed by the coordinator): F1 'One wrapper run':
  the Generate page builds the command list and one wrapper run follows
  it, and `web/job_runner.py` only starts that run detached (it does not
  build or order commands). F2: reset, check-math and the like are
  one-unit registry commands. F3: each API job is a small run of its own.
  F4: `planetgen sector` and `planetgen system` go through the wrapper
  (each a one-command run).
  F3 and F4 merged in #2563 (Core 5, 9:55 PM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane reported, main dd6d46d0): `planetgen sector`, `planetgen
  system` and each API job now run through the wrapper as runs of their
  own. Core 5's own wait-for-turn for API jobs was removed, because
  PERF.153 (#2562) makes every run wait in line. Still open here: F1 and
  F2 and the Generate page, reset, check-math and data-check parts,
  which remain with PERF.123 to PERF.125.
  Prerequisites: PERF.98. Related: PERF.99, PERF.118.

- [ ] **PERF.129 Robust tile caching: the first zoom levels built ahead, tiles stored compressed, built proactively around every visit, kept until the data changes**
  Boss, 2026-10-17, 4:31 PM EDT: "for 8.2 I want to add robust tile
  caching, so that we build out not only the initial galactic view but
  all the normal zoom levels for that view that we can compress and
  serve up to the client immediately on request. Basically I want to
  build out tiles for the first several zoom levels and then I want to
  build it so that system is proactive and when the user visits and zoom
  level it builds and caches all the surrounding tiles and the next zoom
  levels. Then it keeps them until the data changes." What exists (read
  from main, 2026-10-17): `web/lib/tilecache.py` keeps packed tiles on
  disk (`<cache dir>/<db>/<generation>/<tile>.bin`, the PGT1 format of
  `tilepack.py`), answers `/galaxy/tiles` by joining stored bytes, and
  keeps stage and window payloads the same way; freshness is the content
  stamp plus `GET /api/galaxy/changes` (the `modified_at` columns, so
  only the changed tiles are deleted, and a change that cannot be pinned
  to tiles starts a new generation); `prune` deletes the least recently
  written files above `tile_cache.max_mb`; the browser keeps its own
  copy in IndexedDB (MAP.158); `web/warmup.py` warms only the opening
  view's tiles and the galaxy stage; Apache compresses each response at
  send time; the admin health block shows where the cache lives and its
  size. Goal (done when its subitems are): the Galaxy Map answers any
  tile of the first several zoom levels at once from a stored compressed
  copy; a visit to any zoom level builds and caches the surrounding
  tiles and the next level's tiles before they are asked for; every
  stored tile stays until the data under it changes; and an admin can
  see and clear the cache. Subitems: PERF.130 (build the first levels
  ahead), PERF.131 (store and serve compressed), PERF.132 (proactive
  neighbours and next levels on a visit), PERF.133 (keep until the data
  changes), PERF.134 (admin: see and clear). It touches PERF.41 (the
  TILE_FORMAT stamp: a format change must drop the stored tiles once),
  MAP.239 (the tile root rises to the reach, which changes every level's
  geometry, so the build waits for it), MAP.195 (finer tiles leave out
  what a coarser tile sent, which changes what a tile holds), PERF.127
  (`planetgen warm`: the tile build is one of its families, each its own
  command, PERF.120), and the plan commands (a regenerated galaxy
  changes tile content, so the build is a step the wrapper lists after
  the generation commands, never a part of one). Owner: Core 2
  (proposed; the map and cache lane).
  Owner: none for now, returned to the pool (Boss, 7:44 PM EDT
  2026-10-22: work outside 8.1 is paused until 8.1 is complete; Core 2
  held it before; this replaces any earlier owner line).
  Prerequisites: PERF.134.
  Related: PERF.41, PERF.104, PERF.120, PERF.127, MAP.158, MAP.159,
  MAP.195, MAP.239.
  Cut order (Boss, 2026-10-17, 6:48 PM EDT, MAP.250, Decided): the tiles
  stored here are built with halo and satellite-galaxy stars ranked
  below every other star, so a budget cut removes them first; landing
  that rule bumps the tile cache stamp and the cached tiles are rebuilt
  once. The galaxy map lag Boss reported at the same time is MAP.249; if
  its cause is the missing cache, this item is brought forward.
  Boss (2026-10-18, 5:43 PM EDT) widened this goal: the warm-up after
  every update, generation or change runs in phases and goes as deep as
  it can; the stored data may be about 10 times the 40 MB the first tile
  cache cost; the cache is capped at 1 GB by a setting (`cache.max_mb`,
  a slider on the settings page and a key in `config.json`); and every
  list of the site gets a cached index that regenerates when its data
  changes. Filed as PERF.139 (the setting), ADM.97 (the slider),
  PERF.141 (the phased warm-up) and, as one goal with the index and
  lists, DB.79, PERF.140 and UX.141 (issue #2293). Full wording on
  PERF.139.
  Contradiction sweep (Boss's request, 2026-10-18, 5:44 PM EDT; the
  newer note wins, report todo-contradictions-2026-10-18.md): "brought
  forward if its cause is the missing cache" is superseded by Boss's
  card on MAP.249 (2026-10-18, about 8:54 AM EDT, "Both, cut payload
  first"): the tile cache work follows MAP.249's payload cut.
  Decided (Boss, tapped "Skip it" on the card "Store Galaxy Map tiles
  compressed (PERF.131), or skip it?" at 11:27 AM EDT 2026-10-21, tap
  verified on the platform): PERF.131 is skipped and retired. Apache
  keeps compressing at send time (Core 2 measured under 0.1 s a big
  view: a 200-tile view is 3.8 MB packed and 0.8 MB gzipped, gzip 0.03
  to 0.10 s, against 3 to 54 s to build a cold view) and PERF.132
  (#2298) removed the real waits; no new wire format.

- [ ] **PERF.137 Audit the remaining `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` queries: say which serve a big table and move those to keyset paging**
  Found by Core 5 (3:15 AM EDT 2026-10-18 as the lane reported), filed
  by the TODO thread. Keyset paging is done for the Systems, Uncharted
  stars and Phenomena tables (PERF.20 umbrella and PERF.75, #2154);

  finds 16 sites, as candidates only (Core 5 did not trace which serve
  big tables): `db/query.py` lines 214, 501, 576, 618, 857, 898, 1781,
  2270, 2365, 4234 and 6045 (11 queries), `population/model.py` 695, 778
  and 830 (list queries), `db/stats.py` 310 (base names) and
  `queue/work.py` 907 (task listing). The API list routes take `offset`
  (api/routes.py MAX_PAGE_OFFSET) and `web/lib/pagination.py` clamps a
  page past the end. Why it matters: `OFFSET` makes page n cost n times
  as much (measured for the Systems table: rows 0, 20,000, 500,000 and
  1,500,000 take 0.004, 0.13, 5.8 and 12.1 s idle, where a keyset page
  costs 2 ms). Do: for each site, read the caller and the table it pages
  (row count at a full galaxy, from the schema or a measured count) and
  write one line per site: big or small, and the deepest page a user or
  the API can ask for. Move the big ones to the keyset form the three
  finished tables use (`after=<sort key, id>` next to `offset=`) and
  leave the small ones with a one-line comment saying the table stays
  under a few thousand rows. Done: a table of the 16 sites on this item
  with the verdict for each, every big site on keyset paging with a test
  that pages to the end, and the deepest-page time under 50 ms at a full
  galaxy. Owner: Core 5 (proposed, it found the list and wrote the
  PERF.126 and PERF.127 commands); low priority, no version blocker.
  Owner: none for now, returned to the pool (Boss, 7:44 PM EDT
  2026-10-22: work outside 8.1 is paused until 8.1 is complete; Core 5
  held it before; this replaces any earlier owner line).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: PERF.75, PERF.135.

- [ ] **PERF.147 A per-task progress bar with an ETA for any task expected to take, or taking, longer than 15 seconds**
  Boss (2026-10-21, as the coordinator relayed at 8:46 PM EDT): every
  task gets its own progress bar once it is expected to take, or does
  take, longer than 15 seconds, with an ETA blended from the running
  tasks and subtasks and the stored generation statistics, the current
  run weighted more heavily than the stored statistics. It extends the
  existing second bar (the shell scatter bar, shown over 30 seconds,
  with the stored statistics as its starting rate) to every task and
  lowers the threshold to 15 seconds. Do: find where the second bar and
  the stored statistics live, define one task and subtask progress
  record (done, total, started at), compute the ETA as a weighted blend
  whose weight moves from the stored rate to the current run's rate as
  the run proceeds (the weights are named constants), show the bar in
  the command-line output and on the Generate and admin queue pages from
  the same record, and show it only when the expected or actual time
  passes 15 seconds. Done: a task under 15 seconds shows no bar; one
  expected over 15 seconds shows its bar from the start with the
  stored-rate ETA; one that overruns 15 seconds gains the bar when it
  passes the threshold; the ETA moves toward the current run's rate as
  it proceeds (a test with fake clocks and a changed rate); the shell
  scatter bar keeps working through the same record; the Generate page
  and the log show the same numbers. Owner: Bug Hunt (proposed; it has
  PERF.145 queued and the log work, the coordinator decides), after
  PERF.145.
  Boss's even-sized chunk rule is recorded on PERF.148 (the stalled-job
  fix), not here (the coordinator, 8:48 PM EDT 2026-10-21).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: PERF.145, PERF.142, PERF.143, PERF.146.

- [ ] **PERF.166 The mean-system-mass lookup bisects per age (0.2 ms each); a faster form changes the last bits and needs an epoch and Boss's word (bug)**
  Found by the Performance lane in PERF.163 (merged as #2576, relayed
  10:25 PM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane reported); Boss's live observation
  of the 264 s plan stage, so a bug. PERF.163 raised the
  mean-system-mass cache from 512 to 65,536 ages (a plan asks for about
  22,000); `plan --mass 4e9` fell from about 2 minutes (8.0.1960) to
  about 30 s after PERF.146 and about 25 s now, and the plan log ends
  with a step table. The per-age bisection in the mean-system-mass
  lookup costs 0.2 ms per age and 22,000 ages are asked for; replacing
  it with a closed form or an interpolation table would change the last
  bits of the result, so it changes generated values and needs a
  generator epoch (numbered at merge) and Boss's word, and goes to a
  later version unless he says otherwise. Do: measure what the bisection
  costs now (the lane's table says it is small after the cache fix), and
  only if it is worth it, design the replacement with the error bound
  stated and the golden outputs re-baselined. Done: either the measured
  cost is on this item and Boss agrees to leave it, or the replacement
  is merged with its epoch. Owner: none for now (needs Boss's word;
  pool).
  Decided (Boss, 12:27 PM EDT 2026-10-23 (cards, relayed by the
  coordinator)): leave it, option 1. No epoch is spent; the item moves
  to the version 'later' page, phase 3, and is built only if a later
  measurement after PERF.165 shows the saving is worth an epoch.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: PERF.163, PERF.165.

- [ ] **PERF.173 A new-galaxy Generate run dies in stage 5 with "Execution not found in Redis": the worker warm outlives the 90 s execution record (bug)**
  Boss's live observation (relayed 5:18 PM EDT 2026-10-23 by a fix
  thread: 'Recent generate log crashed, investigate, report, and fix';
  filed by the TODO thread). Kind: crash. A new-galaxy Generate run died
  in stage 5 with ValueError: Execution ... not found in Redis after
  saving 5 of 104 sectors. Cause (the fix thread's report,
  /mnt/project-files/reports/generate-redis-crash-2026-10-23.md):
  PERF.146's worker warm ran after RQ created the unit's execution
  record (90 s expiry, first renewal 30 s after the fork), so a warm of
  over a minute on a loaded host left finished units without a record
  and RQ failed them on cleanup, which failed the run. Also found:
  units.unit_failed says RQ calls on_failure only after the retry, which
  is wrong (every failure), so Retry(max=1) only applies to killed
  workers. Fix in progress on branch claude/project-thread-bb2equ
  (cli/worker.py, queue/units.py, tests). Fails on main: yes.
  Reproducer: a new-galaxy run on a loaded host with a worker warm over
  60 s. Do: keep the execution record alive during the warm (renew
  before the warm or warm before the record is created), correct the
  on_failure comment, and add a test that a long warm does not fail a
  unit. Done: a unit whose worker warm takes longer than the record's
  expiry finishes and the run completes, and the test passes. Owner: the
  fix thread (Boss, 5:18 PM EDT 2026-10-23).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: PERF.146, PERF.171.

## DB: Database and schema

DB.1 shipped in 7.35.0 (PR #152). DB.2 to DB.5 done (PR #342, PR #347).

- [ ] **DB.9 Repair a damaged galaxy database from a parity file**
  Boss (same message): "then Phase 1 inject a DB repair using parity
  data stored in a file." Done:
  - Every sector gets a content checksum, the canonical hash of GEN.58's
    fingerprint.
  - A parity file kept outside the database (path in `config.json`)
    holds Reed-Solomon parity over groups of sector exports, so any one
    damaged sector per group can be rebuilt; the group size sets the
    overhead. It is updated whenever sectors are saved or edited, and
    carries its own checksum so damage to it is caught too.
  - `generate.py repair-db` uses DB.8's check to find damaged sectors
    and rebuilds each from the parity file. Where parity can't, and the
    galaxy's seed and version key match the running code (OPS.14), it
    regenerates the sector from its seed and replays its edits from the
    edit log. It re-runs the check and lists anything it could not
    repair.
  - A test damages rows in a copy of a small galaxy, repairs them, and
    gets a passing check.
  Research (2026-10-09, db-check-and-parity-repair.md): (1) replace "the
  canonical hash of GEN.58's fingerprint" with a separate storage
  checksum: SHA-256 over a lossless, id-preserving dump of the stored
  rows, read back after the write. (2) The checksum and the parity
  export omit the columns the daily orbit update rewrites (phases,
  positions, velocities, reflex offsets, binary positions, comet
  anomalies, and a placed object's `sector_id`; the list is in the
  design doc section 5.2). (3) Groups are built from sectors of similar
  export size, far apart in sector id, for an overhead of about 7
  percent. (4) The codec is an in-tree stdlib GF(256) Reed-Solomon
  module (`planetgen/util/rscodec.py`), no new dependency; default G =
  32, m = 2, both in `config.json`. (5) Add the delta update, the record
  format (per-record CRC, per-member checksums) and the stale-record
  decision table. (6) Repair rebuilds the table when a clustered-index
  page is unreadable (dump survivors with `innodb_force_recovery=1`,
  recreate, reload with FK checks off, insert rebuilt sectors with their
  ids). (7) The regenerate-from-seed fallback is split off as the new
  fallback item; this item needs DB.8 only. (8) The test flips bytes in
  an `.ibd` page of a copy while the server is stopped, not `UPDATE`s
  rows. (9) A `dirty` flag on the sector row, set by every writer of
  exported columns (`store.py` direct UPDATEs, `api/edits.py`,
  `db/edits.py`) and cleared after the parity update; listing those
  writers is part of the item. Before DB.19's mass cut `phenomenon_scatter`
  would be 1.17e9 rows and about 161 GB (the earlier 1.6e8 rows and 21 GB
  was an unverified estimate); after the cut it is about 2.7e5 rows.
  Decided (Boss, 2026-10-10 18:44Z, defaults approved; defaults taken):
  after a repair
  the orbit-updated columns come back as generated and the next orbit
  update carries on (a small daily snapshot of ids, phases and sector
  only if exact positions matter); G = 32, m = 2; repairing a bad
  clustered-index page may mean restarting the database server with
  `innodb_force_recovery=1`.
  Split (2026-10-16, Boss 1:07 PM EDT: look at each item for smaller
  chunks and shared work): this item is now the umbrella and is done
  when its subitems are: DB.43, DB.44, DB.45, DB.46, DB.47, DB.48. The
  largest item of the slice: a stdlib codec, a schema change, a checksum
  that every writer of exported columns must respect, a parity file kept
  current on every save, a repair command, and a table rebuild for an
  unreadable clustered-index page (nine research points in its text).
  Prerequisite GEN.57 dropped (2026-10-16 review): only the
  regenerate-from-seed fallback, DB.17, needs it; the parity half needs
  DB.8 only.
  Owner: Core 1 (Boss's lanes to 8.1, 2026-10-17, 10:06 AM EDT; lane
  assignment
  /mnt/project-files/reports/core1-5-lanes-to-8-1-2026-10-17.md). This replaces any earlier owner line on this item.
  Prerequisites: DB.45, DB.46, DB.47, DB.48.
  Design: [docs/design/generation/reproducible-galaxies.md](design/generation/reproducible-galaxies.md)

- [ ] **DB.29 update.sh and every database migration refuse to start while jobs are active, unless --yes is passed or the user confirms cancelling them**
  Boss, 2026-10-15 02:55Z: "Add TODO item, when migrating the database
  to a new version, if there are active jobs, ask the user to cancel the
  jobs first before changing anything." Widened by Boss, 02:56Z: "In
  fact, anytime update is run, it won't start without either --yes
  passed OR if the user specifically confirms they want to cancel all
  jobs prior to starting the upgrade or install." Done: before it
  changes anything, update.sh (every install and every upgrade, not only
  runs that migrate) and the migrate command check for active jobs
  (running or queued generation runs and other background jobs). With
  none, they proceed as before. With any, they list them and stop until
  either `--yes` was passed, or the user types an explicit confirmation
  that all active jobs may be cancelled; only then are the jobs
  cancelled, and then the install or upgrade starts. Boss, 02:59Z: "the
  update script needs to know if it's being run either from systemd or
  cron, and if it has, assume no unless --yes is passed. Or say 30
  seconds of waiting for input and it assumes no and cancels the
  update." So update.sh detects a run from systemd or cron (no person
  at the keyboard) and then assumes "no": it changes nothing and exits
  non-zero unless `--yes` was passed. When it does prompt, 30 seconds
  without an answer count as "no": it changes nothing and exits
  non-zero. Without `--yes` and without a terminal to ask on, it does
  the same.
  update.sh still never edits the user's Redis configuration (OPS.48).
  A test covers each path (no jobs, jobs and `--yes`, jobs and a typed
  confirmation, jobs and no answer within 30 seconds, jobs and a run
  from systemd or cron), and the check is the one place every
  migration goes through.
  Dependency: how the active jobs are read depends on the work queue
  steps. PERF.96 (run record and counters in Redis, done, PR #1553)
  supplies the library call that lists active runs, which the check
  uses; and PERF.99 supplies the cancel through the stop
  command, after which the check uses them. PERF.100 (which deletes the
  old work tables with a migration) must pass through this check too.
  Owner: Database, after DB.28 (done, PR #1476) and before PERF.100.
  Prerequisites: PERF.99. Related: PERF.95 (done, PR #1506), PERF.96
  (done, PR #1553), PERF.99, PERF.100, OPS.48, DB.18, DB.27 (done, PR
  #1446), DB.28 (done, PR #1476).
  Owner: Core 1, in its bug phase after the global top chain (Boss,
  2026-10-16, 2:43 PM EDT: "Core 1 will start working on bugs after";
  order set at 3:00 PM EDT: non-test bugs, then the database-version
  test failures, then the failures that hit full runs, then the one-off
  load flakes). Fix the cause; no skipping or quarantine.
  Owner: Core 5 (Boss's lanes to 8.1, 2026-10-17, 10:06 AM EDT; lane
  assignment
  /mnt/project-files/reports/core1-5-lanes-to-8-1-2026-10-17.md). This replaces any earlier owner line on this item.
  Order on Core 5's lane (Boss's card, 2026-10-17, 10:57 PM EDT as the

  UX.122, UX.123, TEST.183) comes after the command follow-ups, not before them, with PERF.118

- [ ] **DB.40 Parity data backup part: the parity file of the DB repair copied into the backup archive**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:59 PM and 2:00 PM EDT): "let's add backups of the
  control DB and backups of the parity data for DB repair." and "All
  those should be bz2 tarballed together." Boss (2:00 PM EDT): "we also
  have to build a way to use that data so build that out and let's make
  this targetted for v9.0 so incorporate the chain for these (restore /
  repair using backups) with that due date. Settings page is v8.1".
  Target 8.9 (the backups and repair chain, umbrella ADM.91); the
  settings page and the settings backups stay in 8.1 (ADM.83 to ADM.85).
  All backup pieces are parts of one `.tar.bz2` archive (ADM.87);
  retention is `settings.backups_kept` (default 20, 1 to 200). DB.9
  keeps parity for every sector in an append-only parity file outside
  the database (path in `config.json`). A damaged database is only
  repairable with a parity file that matches it, so the file is a backup
  part, written to `parity/`: the copy is taken under the parity
  writer's lock and cuts at the last complete record (the file is an
  append-only log of self-describing records with a header scan, so no
  index is stored); it can be switched off for a very large galaxy with
  the option `settings.backup_parity` (default on), and the manifest
  records its size and the sector count it covers. Done: the part
  registered with ADM.87, the lock-held copy under a concurrent save,
  and the size and coverage in the manifest (the restore is DB.41).
  Prerequisites: DB.46. Related: ADM.85, DB.8, DB.17.

  ARCHIVE` and the backup list use it. Done: a restore on a fixture

- [ ] **DB.42 Repair the galaxy from an archive: `repair-db --from-archive` uses the parity part of a backup when the live parity file is missing or damaged**
  Boss (2:00 PM EDT): "we also have to build a way to use that data so

  chain, umbrella ADM.91); the settings page and the settings backups
  stay in 8.1 (ADM.83 to ADM.85). All backup pieces are parts of one
  `.tar.bz2` archive (ADM.87); retention is `settings.backups_kept`
  (default 20, 1 to 200). The galaxy database itself is not in the
  archive (too large; it can be regenerated from the seed, DB.17, and
  repaired from parity, DB.9). `repair-db` of DB.9 reads the live parity
  file; with `--from-archive ARCHIVE` (or the choice on the repair page)
  it reads the archive's parity part instead when the live file is
  missing, damaged or newer than the damage. It applies the stale-record
  decision table against the live database, rebuilds every damaged
  sector it can, and lists the sectors it cannot repair (a stale record,
  more than m members of a group lost) for the seed regeneration of
  DB.17, with a report of what came from which source. Done: tests on a
  copy of a small galaxy: the live parity file deleted and the damage
  repaired from the archive, a group that lost too many members listed
  and handed to DB.17, and a stale archive recompute that does not
  damage a healthy sector.
  Prerequisites: DB.41, DB.9, DB.17. Related: DB.9, DB.17, ADM.91.

- [ ] **DB.45 Storage checksum and the dirty flag: the export, the checksum and every writer**
  Split from DB.9 (2026-10-16, Boss 1:07 PM EDT: look at each item for
  smaller chunks and shared work). Compute the sector's storage checksum
  as SHA-256 over a lossless, id-preserving dump of its stored rows,
  read back after the write, leaving out the columns the daily orbit
  update rewrites (phases, positions, velocities, reflex offsets, binary
  positions, comet anomalies, a placed object's `sector_id`; list in
  design section 5.2). Every writer of exported columns sets
  `parity_dirty` in its own transaction: the direct UPDATEs in
  `db/store.py` (names, positions, velocity), `api/edits.py` and
  `db/edits.py`; finding every writer is part of this item. DB.8's check
  reads the checksum and reports a dirty sector as "unprotected", not
  damaged. Why: the parity file can only be correct if a changed row is
  always noticed. Done: the export and checksum, every writer marked,
  and tests: each writer sets the flag; an orbit update does not change
  the checksum; a flipped stored value is reported as damage and a dirty
  sector as unprotected.
  Owner: Core 1 (Boss's lanes to 8.1, 2026-10-17, 10:06 AM EDT; lane
  assignment
  /mnt/project-files/reports/core1-5-lanes-to-8-1-2026-10-17.md). This replaces any earlier owner line on this item.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: DB.9.

- [ ] **DB.46 The parity file: groups, records, a delta update on every save and the stale-record rule**
  Split from DB.9 (2026-10-16, Boss 1:07 PM EDT: look at each item for
  smaller chunks and shared work). A parity file kept outside the
  database (path in `config.json`) with G = 32 members and m = 2 parity
  blocks per group (both in `config.json`), groups formed at save time
  from sectors of one export-size class that are far apart in sector id
  (the W = 256 rule, shrinking for small galaxies); an append-only log
  of self-describing records (magic, format version, group id, `seq`,
  per-member address, length and checksum, parity bytes, CRC32C), an
  in-memory index rebuilt by a header scan, compaction as a function.
  Each save updates the group's parity from the member's before-image
  inside the saving transaction (`P_j' = P_j xor c_ji x (old xor new)`),
  after checking the before-image against its old checksum, then clears
  `parity_dirty`. The stale-record decision table of design 5.6 is code.
  Why: this is the part that makes repair possible and it must cost
  milliseconds per save. Done: the file, the update on save, and tests:
  save, edit and delete keep parity equal to a fresh encode; a torn tail
  loses nothing; a stale record is recomputed, not treated as damage;
  overhead is about 7 percent on a 1,000-sector fixture.
  Owner: Core 1 (Boss's lanes to 8.1, 2026-10-17, 10:06 AM EDT; lane
  assignment
  /mnt/project-files/reports/core1-5-lanes-to-8-1-2026-10-17.md). This replaces any earlier owner line on this item.
  Prerequisites: DB.45. Related: DB.9.

- [ ] **DB.48 repair-db: rebuild the table when a clustered-index page is unreadable**
  Split from DB.9 (2026-10-16, Boss 1:07 PM EDT: look at each item for
  smaller chunks and shared work). When a page of the `sectors`
  clustered index cannot be read, rebuild the table: restart the
  database server with `innodb_force_recovery=1` (the command says so
  first and asks), dump the surviving rows, recreate the table, reload

  present.

  central object (as binary stars are done now); every object other than
  the central object can be another system with that object as its
  central object, down to small objects that get no satellites; all
  objects follow the same physics, so the origin of the system's space

- [ ] **DB.84 Every schema change on `sectors` rebuilds the whole table because of its FULLTEXT index: decide how the later DB items pay for it**
  Found by Blocker 2 (about 4:02 AM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane reported,
  DB.44), filed by the TODO thread. The FULLTEXT index on `sectors`
  forces `ALGORITHM=COPY` on a MySQL `ALTER TABLE`, so DB.44's two
  columns were added by a full table rebuild in one migration instead of
  the INSTANT form the DB.18 helpers prefer. On a large galaxy that is a
  long `update.sh` step and needs free disk for a second copy of the
  table. Every later migration that touches `sectors` pays the same
  cost. Do: decide with the DB items chain lane and Boss's defaults (no
  question card needed unless the choice changes a feature): the default
  is to batch every remaining `sectors` column change into as few
  migrations as possible, say the rebuild cost in the migration
  docstring and in the update.sh output, and keep the FULLTEXT index;
  the other choice is to move the FULLTEXT index to a side table so
  `sectors` can use INSTANT again. Done: the choice is written in
  docs/design/architecture/architecture.md and the DB.18 helper docstring, and every
  open item that adds a `sectors` column is checked against it. Owner:
  not assigned (the DB items chain lane after its listed order).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: DB.18, DB.44.

  same commands and options as a local run (`sector`, `galaxy` modes,
  `plan`, the bright-star scatter and backfill, `population`); it asks
  the server for what it needs first (the galaxy's seed and skeleton,
  which sectors are already filled, the id and name state), generates
  on the local machine with all its workers, then uploads the results
  in batches to new API routes that check the key, validate each batch
  (ADM.5's validator), refuse sectors that were filled meanwhile, save
  them the same way a server-side run does (names, ids, bright-star
  levels, caches and tiles invalidated), and report what was added. A
  remote run appears in the job tree and job page (ADM.10, PR #294; ADM.12, PR #285) like
  a server-side one. Boss's answers (2026-10-01 19:28Z):
  - Generate and keep in memory: the local machine needs no database of
    its own.
  - The name indexes and id state are downloaded from the API once, for
    local use, so the run doesn't keep calling the API for them (the
    server reserves id blocks and claims the sectors for the run).
  - Uploads and downloads are compressed (gzip, bz2 or similar): some
    compression time is worth faster transfers.
  - Fully resumable: the local machine caches on disk every API call it
    means to send until the server confirms it; the server keeps a
    buffer of everything it receives, stages it, and writes to the
    database in a controlled way only complete units (a complete star
    system, a complete sector). This probably needs database changes
    so staged data can be stored and flagged incomplete until it is.
  - The local version must match the server's API version (API.4 and
    API.5).
  Boss's answers (2026-10-01 19:32Z):
  - Only an admin's API key can upload; user-level keys can read but
    never upload (API.6).

  - Reserved ids and claimed sectors stay reserved until the upload
    finishes or an admin clears it; nothing else may use them in the
    meantime. Admins see and clear incomplete uploads on their own page
    (ADM.13).
  - The server checks every upload and has the final say on what is
    written to the database (API.8).

  Boss (2026-10-01 19:32Z): "the API will have to have a reliable method
  of syncing and making sure uploaded data is verified good before it
  is finalized in the DB, the server has the final say in how items are
  added to the database." Done: the client and server agree, by batch
  and by unit (a star system, a sector), on what has been sent and
  received, with checksums, so nothing is lost or written twice; every
  staged unit is checked on the server before it is finalized

  names unique, and the physics checks of ADM.5's validator); the
  server finalizes a unit in one transaction or rejects it with the
  reasons, and may correct what it can (renaming a clashing name,
  re-running derived values) rather than trusting the client's copy.
  Question (decided below): which corrections the server makes on its
  own, and
  which reject the unit so the client regenerates it.
  Research (2026-10-09, api-design-standards.md): adopt the auto-correct
  versus reject rule (design doc 7.4) as the default answer: correct
  only a clashing name and pure derived columns; reject everything else;
  the server returns a rename map; a rejection does not release the
  claim.
  Decided (2026-10-10): Boss (19:16Z, Accept all): the server auto-fixes
  only a clashing name and purely derived columns, and rejects
  everything else so the client regenerates it.

  one-transaction finalize and the limited auto-fix are the unit
  finalizer ADM.82, built in 8.6 for change plans. This item is what

  requests should have a browser UA string saying the software, its
  version number, and the API version being used that fits industry
  standards." Read as (default taken, the coordinator's reading): every
  outgoing HTTP request the software makes sends a `User-Agent` in the
  RFC 9110 form of product tokens with a comment, for example
  `PlanetGen/8.0.1721 (+https://github.com/dwhagar/planetGen)
  PlanetGen-API/1.4`, the first token the release from
  `planetgen/_version.py`, the comment the project URL, the last token
  the API version from `planetgen/api/version.py`. One function builds
  the string (the only place that spells it), so a test checks the
  format and that it follows both versions when they change; the
  outgoing callers are `web/lib/apiclient.py`, `wiki/mediawiki.py`,
  `wiki/wikijs.py`, the CLI tools that fetch, any later API client (the
  remote generate client of API.30) and the data downloads at build time
  of the gap-filling plan (GEN.439, GEN.440, GEN.463, GEN.413, GEN.414,
  GEN.485, GEN.499 and the atmosphere data of group X9), which must use
  it. Requests the browser's own front end makes cannot set
  `User-Agent`, so the page JavaScript that calls the API sends the
  existing API version header (`API_VERSION_HEADER`,
  `X-PlanetGen-API-Version`) with the same API version instead, and the
  server keeps logging both (API.15). Done: one function builds the user
  agent from the two versions; every outgoing request path above uses
  it; the front end's API calls carry the API version header; a test
  pins the format (valid product tokens, release, URL comment, API
  version), that no outgoing path builds its own string, and that a
  version bump changes it; the API docs and the data-download design
  (docs/design/research/gap-filling-plan.md 6.5) name it.
  Owner: Core 2, proposed (the interface housekeeping line beside API.15
  and API.26; not asked yet, the coordinator tells Core 2 when it
  reaches the item).
  Detail (Blocker 1, 2:47 AM EDT 2026-10-18 as the lane reported):
  GEN.548 adds `planetgen/util/user_agent.py` with `user_agent()`, the
  one function that builds the identifying User-Agent string; this item
  reuses it instead of writing a second one (it is on the GEN.548
  branch, so it is on main once GEN.548 merges).
  Owner: Core 1 (8.1 queue, Boss, 7:44 PM EDT 2026-10-22; the queue is
  in reports/8-1-core-queues-2026-10-22.md; this replaces any earlier
  owner line).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: API.5, API.15, API.30.

- [ ] **test_fuzz_web_routes fails on a machine that has a real database named planetgen_control: every galaxy route answers 500 for db=planetgen_control (bug)**
  Found by the Performance lane (relayed 4:15 AM EDT 2026-10-23 as the
  lane reported) in its gate for PERF.164 as a failure of
  test_get_routes_survive_hostile_query[GET /api/containers]; filed by
  the TODO thread under the first reading (a route that answers 500 to a
  hostile query), and corrected by Performance (relayed 6:13 AM EDT
  2026-10-23 as the lane reported): it is not an app bug. That lane's
  MySQL held a real database named planetgen_control (its plan and suite
  runs create it). The fuzz test sends db=planetgen_control on purpose
  (security #47), and under the test fixtures the configured control
  database has a different name, so the real planetgen_control resolves
  as an ordinary galaxy schema and every galaxy route answers 500 with
  (1146, "Table 'planetgen_control.galaxy_containers' doesn't exist").
  That was 39 failures in its PERF.165 gate: every GET route in
  test_fuzz_web_routes.py and test_api_bad_input_is_a_clean_4xx for
  /api/sectors?db=planetgen_control. With the database dropped the file
  passes in full (1992 passed with the other two files). Bug Hunt could
  not reproduce it because its machine has no planetgen_control. Kind:
  test depends on the machine (flaky by environment). Frequency: every
  run on a machine that has that database. Do: make the fixture make the
  real control name unresolvable as a galaxy (or have the test create
  and exclude it), so the test no longer depends on the machine lacking
  that name. Done: test_fuzz_web_routes.py and
  test_api_bad_input_is_a_clean_4xx pass on a machine that holds a
  database named planetgen_control. Owner: Bug Hunt (proposed by the
  TODO thread).
  Prerequisites: none. Related: DB.85, TEST.290.

## ADM: Admin tools

- [ ] **ADM.13 Incomplete uploads page**
  Boss (2026-10-01 19:32Z): "Admin will have to have a page where they
  can see incomplete uploads and clear them but reserved sectors by ID
  cannot be used if an upload isn't finished." Done: an admin-only page
  lists the remote uploads of API.3 that have not finished: who started
  them, when, the sectors and id blocks they reserved, how much is
  staged and verified (API.8), and when the client last sent anything.
  Clearing one, confirmed and written to the admin activity log, throws
  away its staged data and releases its sectors and id blocks; until
  then nothing else (a server-side run, another upload) may use them.
  Part of, or linked from, the job page (ADM.10, PR #294). Question
  (decided below): should
  an upload with no contact for a long time be flagged as stale on the
  page?
  Research (2026-10-09, api-design-standards.md): the stale flag
  defaults to 3 days without contact and only flags; the page reads
  `upload_runs`, `upload_units` and `upload_claims`.
  Decided (2026-10-10): Boss (19:16Z, Accept all): flag an upload that
  has been silent for 3 days; flag only, never auto-clear.

- [ ] **ADM.32 Add a star system to a sector: at the emptiest spot, at given coordinates, or at random outside every Hill sphere**
  Boss (2026-10-07 11:47Z): "Need a way to add a single star system to a
  sector, the computer will place in the area of lowest density if it
  can without crossing the hill sphere of another object, if the object
  cannot be placed then it will gracefully error out." And: "Add the
  ability to insert a sector or move a stand-alone sector into some
  location in a sector of admin's choosing.  They can specify
  coordinates (in 3 different ways) of the star system relative to the
  center of the sector or center of the galaxy (either needs to be an
  option).  The admin should also be able to select random placement
  within the sector so long as it is not in a hill sphere, the system
  will not move existing stars without admin approval. Admin can also
  choose to have the computer put the new star system in the least
  populated area, basically the spot that is farthest from everything
  that you can get within the sector." Done: from the sector page, an
  admin adds a new or existing stand-alone system by (1) the emptiest
  point (farthest from every object), (2) coordinates in Cartesian,
  cylindrical or spherical form relative to the sector centre or the
  galaxy centre (GEN.74), or (3) random; no placement may fall inside
  another object's Hill sphere, nothing existing moves without the admin
  confirming, and a placement that can't be made fails with a message
  and changes nothing.
  Moved to phase 3, Move and orbit, before ADM.71, and built on the
  shell and the plan engine: the action becomes the "add" plan operation
  that goes through approval; ADM.71 takes the placement functions from
  here and narrows to the move operation and the drag (2026-10-16
  review).
  Prerequisites: ADM.58, ADM.65, ADM.66, ADM.82.

- [ ] **ADM.36 Change an object's trajectory vector**
  Boss (2026-10-07 11:47Z): "Give the user the ability to change an
  object's trajectory vector." Done: an admin sets a body's velocity
  vector (in any frame the position object supports) from its detail
  screen; the change is validated (escape, collisions), logged, and used
  by the next orbital update.
  Research (2026-10-09, collisions-and-mergers.md): after an admin edits
  a velocity vector, recompute the osculating elements,
  `next_update_due` and Hill and cover-list membership at once (the next
  run could be far off); report if the new vector makes the orbit
  unbound. The validation step ("escape, collisions") computes the swept
  path against stored bodies and shows the predicted event; admin-aimed
  hits are the realistic way to see the collision code run.
  Moved to phase 3, Move and orbit, before ADM.72 (2026-10-16 review):
  it builds the orbit-edit operation once (state vector to elements in
  any frame the position object supports, the escape and swept-path
  collision validation, the recompute, the unbound report) as a plan
  operation; ADM.72 adds the element form and the moons following on the
  same operation.
  Prerequisites: ADM.58, ADM.65, ADM.66.

- [ ] **ADM.58 Change plan engine: operations, the effect diff and the plan states, as a library**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:07 PM EDT), headline of 8.6 (ADM.57): the admin
  has complete control; the world adjusts to what the admin wants, after
  the admin approves the generation plan. A plan is an ordered list of
  operations (move an object, set an aspect, regenerate with a keep set,
  add, remove) on stored objects. Build `planetgen/admin/plans.py`: the
  operation types, validation of each against the stored object (Hill
  spheres, spacing, bounds), the computed effect diff (every row that
  would change, with before and after, and every object touched
  indirectly), the state machine (draft, requested, proposed, approved,
  applied, undone, stale, rejected, withdrawn: `requested` is a plan
  someone below the approving role submitted, used by 10.0 and built
  here so no state is added later; an admin's own plan goes from draft
  to proposed and the same admin confirms it, with no second approver,
  Boss 2026-10-16, 1:49 PM EDT; every transition records who and in
  which role) and the stale check (a plan is stale when any
  object it touches changed after the plan was proposed). An operation
  serialises in the versioned envelope the remote upload uses
  (`StarSystem.to_dict()`, API.13), so a plan and an upload describe a
  system the same way. Pure Python over loaded objects, no database, so
  it can be tested on its own. Done: the library with unit tests for
  every operation kind, the diff and the stale check.
  Staleness (2026-10-16 review): "changed" means changed by an edit (the
  journal row or an edit-version stamp per object), not by the nightly
  orbital update; a pending move or orbit plan re-bases its before
  values after an update has run and the approval screen shows the
  drift. Add "orbital update movement" to the tests.
  Waits for 8.6 (Boss, 2026-10-16, 3:00 PM EDT: a global top blocker
  that is not started before its version); no lane yet.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: ADM.57, ADM.6, ADM.7, ADM.8.
  Design: [docs/design/interface/edit-everything.md](design/interface/edit-everything.md)

- [ ] **ADM.60 Apply, undo and audit a plan: one job, one activity-log entry per operation**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:07 PM EDT), headline of 8.6 (ADM.57): the admin
  has complete control; the world adjusts to what the admin wants, after
  the admin approves the generation plan. Each unit is written through
  the unit finalizer (ADM.82). An approved plan is applied, under the
  approver's identity, as a visible queue job (the journal and the
  activity log name the requester and the approver) (the Generate page
  job log): operations run in order inside
  one transaction per sector, each writes its journal rows and an
  activity-log entry, and a failure rolls the whole plan back and leaves
  it proposed with the reason. An applied plan can be undone as long as
  nothing newer touched the same objects: undo is the inverse plan built
  from the stored before values. Apply refuses while the update guard is
  on (maintenance, a running update, or the orbital update). Done:
  apply, undo and audit with tests, including a failed apply that
  changes nothing and an undo that restores every stored row.
  Prerequisites: ADM.59. Related: ADM.57, OPS.41, ADM.82.
  Design: [docs/design/interface/edit-everything.md](design/interface/edit-everything.md)

- [ ] **ADM.61 Edits survive repair and regeneration: replay the journal after a sector is rebuilt from its seed or from parity**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:07 PM EDT), headline of 8.6 (ADM.57): the admin
  has complete control; the world adjusts to what the admin wants, after
  the admin approves the generation plan. A sector rebuilt from its seed
  (DB.17) or repaired from a parity file (DB.9) would lose every admin
  edit, and GEN.57 says a sector depends only on the seed, the version
  and its address. Keep that rule: the generated sector is the base and
  the edit journal is replayed over it, in order, so the rebuilt sector
  equals the edited one. A journal row that no longer applies (the base
  changed with a generator epoch) is listed for the admin, not dropped.
  Done: replay after both rebuild paths, a test that a sector with edits
  rebuilds to the same stored rows, and the list of rows that cannot
  replay.
  Prerequisites: ADM.60, DB.17, DB.9. Related: DB.9, DB.17,
  GEN.57, GEN.59.
  Design: [docs/design/interface/edit-everything.md](design/interface/edit-everything.md)

- [ ] **ADM.64 Keep-or-regenerate resolution: from the admin's marks to the exact set of aspects redrawn**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:07 PM EDT), headline of 8.6 (ADM.57): the admin
  has complete control; the world adjusts to what the admin wants, after

  Resolve the marks into what the generator redraws: a regenerated

- [ ] **ADM.65 Locks: keep marks that stay on an object or one of its aspects, shown on the pages and honoured by every plan**
  Boss (2026-10-16, 1:07 PM EDT), headline of 8.6 (ADM.57): the admin
  has complete control; the world adjusts to what the admin wants, after
  the admin approves the generation plan. An admin can lock an object or
  one aspect of it (a star's class, a planet's orbit). Every plan treats
  a locked aspect as kept and refuses an operation that would change it
  unless the admin lifts the lock inside the plan; the system page and
  the maps mark locked objects. The plan engine takes a lock predicate
  and this item registers it, so every plan refuses an operation on a
  locked aspect. Done: lock and unlock from the object page, the
  registered predicate, the marks, and a test that the plan engine
  refuses a change to a locked aspect (the regeneration, rearrangement
  and density items each test their own).
  Prerequisites: ADM.62, ADM.58. Related: ADM.57.
  Design: [docs/design/interface/edit-everything.md](design/interface/edit-everything.md)

## SEC: Security

The login protection of 2026-10-01 (SEC.1, SEC.20 to
SEC.28: the always-on activity log, per-address and per-username
lockouts, trusted devices, the password blocklist and hashing cost,
two-factor sign-in and the fail2ban example) shipped in PRs #217, #220
and #221.

Design: [docs/design/operations/login-brute-force-protection.md](design/operations/login-brute-force-protection.md)

- [ ] **SEC.33 Release gate: a full security code audit of the whole code base, done before every major or minor version change (8.1 first)**
  Boss, 2026-10-21, 5:10 PM EDT: before 8.1 is stamped finished there
  must be a full security code audit, and it MUST be done before every
  single major or minor version change (8.1, 8.2 and on to 9.0 and 10.0;
  the 8.0.NNNN builds are exempt). One standing item: it stays open and
  is re-run for each major or minor version change, never retired.
  Confirmed and narrowed to this wording by Boss, 8:01 PM EDT
  2026-10-22: required whenever the major or minor number changes, not
  for build numbers. Scope: every route, API
  endpoint and form; sign-in, sessions, cookies, CSRF, rate limits and
  lockouts; authorization and every admin page; all SQL and any string
  built into a query; file, path and upload handling and the tile cache
  and jobs directory; the stored-XSS and output-escaping paths in
  templates and JavaScript; the Content-Security-Policy and headers;
  secrets, config and settings handling; the dependency list and its
  known vulnerabilities (pip and npm lockfiles); the install, update and
  deployment scripts and the systemd and Apache or nginx examples; the
  Redis and job-queue inputs; and anything new since the last pass (use
  git log since the last audited release). Run the repository's own
  static checks and add a scanner pass where one can run without the
  network. Done: for the release, a dated report
  (/mnt/project-files/reports/release-audit-security-<version>.md,
  linked from the goal issue and logged on this item as 'Release log:
  <version>, <EDT date and time>, <commit>') that names the commit
  audited, lists what was covered and what was not, and files every
  finding as its own item (a high or critical finding blocks the release
  until fixed and merged; the rest are filed with an owner). The release
  is not stamped while the report for its version is missing, or while a
  finding it marks blocking is open. Proposed owner: its own thread,
  started when the version nears close (8.1: after the whole-sphere
  audits TEST.185, TEST.184, TEST.159 and TEST.160 merge, so the audit
  sees the final code); it must not be the lane that wrote the code
  under audit.
  Ordering (TODO thread, 6:40 PM EDT 2026-10-21): this audit runs after
  the performance profile PERF.146 so it sees the final code.
  Owner: a new audit thread, started when PERF.146 closes (Boss, 7:44
  PM EDT 2026-10-22: all five cores on 8.1; this replaces any earlier
  owner line).
  Method: follow /mnt/project-files/reports/audit-playbook-2026-10-22.md
  (the coordinator, relayed 7:58 PM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane's clock
  reads).
  Gate rule (Boss, 8:04 PM EDT 2026-10-22): the
  version is not stamped while a confirmed Critical or High finding is
  open; Mediums are filed with owners; data loss, corruption or broken
  seed reproducibility counts as High. This holds unless Boss
  specifically authorizes an exception.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: TEST.261.

## TEST: The test suite

From the test suite plan of 2026-10-01 (Boss: "build me a list of TEST
items (TEST.x) to build our testing suite to cover all edge cases, and
prepare to do another solid full on bug hunt. Don't implement just plan
for it"). Each item ends with its areas in brackets. "Suspected bug"
means read from the code, not reproduced yet; the bug hunt confirms or
clears each one.

### Infrastructure and CI

- [ ] **TEST.111 test_ensure_sector_generated_creates_then_reuses_the_same_sector fails in a busy parallel run (bug)**
  Reported by Bugfixes lane 1 (2026-10-09 23:32Z):
  `test_ensure_sector_generated_creates_then_reuses_the_same_sector`
  failed once in a busy parallel full-suite run and passed alone, with
  no change to the code it covers. Done: the cause is found (a shared
  sector address or timing under load is the first thing to check) and
  the test is made robust without skipping or loosening it, or the
  product bug it hides is fixed. Related: TEST.71, TEST.73, OPS.19.
  Note (2026-10-09): Bugfixes lane 1 (PR #955, 2026-10-10): no repro in
  15 loaded runs; the test's asserts now print the results, so the next
  failure names the cause. Stays open until it recurs and is fixed, or
  Boss closes it.
  Decided (Test Suite Rebuild thread, 2026-10-14 14:04Z, list in
  /mnt/project-files/test-suite-rebuild/test-fix-decisions.md): fold
  into the rebuild, no separate hunt; stage 1 keeps each failure's
  traceback and re-runs it alone, stage 3 gives each worker its own
  database; closed after 5 clean full runs after stage 3, or fixed from
  the captured traceback on recurrence. Owner: Quality (2026-10-15, took over from the Test Suite Rebuild thread).
  Recurrence (Quality, 2026-10-15, 4:56 PM EDT run): the test hung, not
  just failed, and looks like GEN.232's uncapped path integration of a
  fast star. Core fixes GEN.232; Quality re-checks this test after it
  and closes this item on 5 clean full runs as decided.
  Quality confirms (2026-10-15, combined run, MySQL 8.0.46): the test
  runs past 900 s and fails alone on main, in db/sector_paths.py settle
  and physics/sector_path.py integrate_path, _simplify and hermite; it
  points at GEN.232.
  Intermittent (Quality, 2026-10-15): it passed in the 6:13 PM EDT run
  on the same code that timed out alone at 4:20 PM EDT, so it is not
  deterministic; GEN.232 merged in #1660, so Quality re-checks it in the
  next full run.
  Owner: Bug Hunt (proposed; Boss started the lane at 10:20 PM EDT with

- [ ] **TEST.190 A failing session fixture makes every dependent test wait its full 900 s timeout: fail the dependents at once (bug)**
  Found by a lane (2026-10-16), filed by the TODO thread. When a
  session-scoped fixture (for example the browser-test server) fails to
  start, each test that needs it waits its whole 900 s timeout before
  failing, so one fixture failure costs hours of the run. Done: a
  fixture that fails marks its dependents as errors at once (pytest does
  that already for a raised error, so the cause is in how the fixture
  waits; find it and fix it), and a test shows a dead fixture ends the
  run in seconds. Fails on main: yes. Frequency: whenever a session
  fixture fails. Reproducer: make the server fixture raise after its
  start and time the run.
  Owner: Bug Hunt (proposed, Boss's lane started 10:20 PM EDT).
  Status (2026-10-16, 11:43 PM EDT, Bug Hunt as relayed): could not
  reproduce as described. pytest already fails the tests that depend on
  a failed session fixture at once, so the 900 s wait this item
  describes did not appear. Needed next time: The run log that shows
  dependents waiting their full timeout, and the fixture that failed
  first. Running log: the comments on issue #1694.
  Prerequisites: none. Related: TEST.111.

  Boss (2026-10-17, 1:40 AM EDT, typed in the project chat): "We have to
  add to our composition plans that what I'd like to do is for each
  composition have a list of possibilities with their weighted
  probabilities (for all compositions, each category will have a table
  of possibilities and their associated values). So, list items will be
  gated, each table line has a list of supported planet or object
  classes and then we draw composition based on the composition
  probabilities to add up to 100%." Boss's check: the weights of the
  rows that pass a class's gate add up to 100 percent. Do: one test
  walks the registry of the possibility-table loader (GEN.472), so a
  table added later is covered without a change to the test, and for
  every table and every class in the code's class lists builds the gated
  set at a sweep of stars and formation distances (the weight functions'
  arguments), and checks that the normalised weights add up to 1.0
  within 1e-12, that the gate of no class is empty, that no row has a
  weight below zero or without a source and a licence, that the `open`
  weights are reported and their number does not grow without a note,
  and that a table in the code which is not registered fails the test
  (no composition table outside the loader). It also checks the second
  sum: the fractions or partial pressures a drawn row supplies add up to
  one for a seeded sample of every class. Done: the test passes on every

  (GEN.623).

- [ ] **TEST.244 Tests: re-primary and reparent invariants, frame round trips, momentum conservation, a moon's velocity as the sum of its hops, a locked body's rate follows a primary change**
  Part of the unified orbited-body plan (GEN.550; design note
  docs/design/architecture/unified-system-barycentre.md, decided: Boss's nine cards
  S10 to S18 on the primary-first rule, the point-in-space frames and
  motion and spin, tapped between 12:30 and 12:32 AM EDT on 2026-10-18
  (as the coordinator relayed with the wake times converted), every one
  the recommended option: S10 the original values are the origin values
  (birth mass, age, [Fe/H], composition, formation distance) plus the
  orbit-geometry draws, and the present state is recomputed about the
  new primary; S11 the heaviest is found by the total mass of each
  branch (a sub-system counts as the sum of its parts), ties under 1e-9
  relative keep the draw order; S12 when the heaviest changes in
  simulated time the step runs once at the event (merger, capture,
  ejection), state-preserving, so no body jumps; S13 trajectories are an
  analytic two-body orbit per frame with mu including the member's own
  mass, and the outer system's tide is a stability gate (Hill fraction,
  triple and Kozai screens); S14 a frame request names any of the named
  frames or any other point, found through the lowest common ancestor;
  S15 a point has a live parent link with a versioned cache and the
  copied anchors and the three `carry_*` calls go; S16 the point holds a
  kinematic record (position, velocity, spin axis and rate, mass with
  mu, epoch and next-due) with identity, radius and age beside it in the
  core; S17 spin is a unit axis plus an angular rate in rad/s; S18
  speed, axial tilt, galactic orbital period and phase, rotation period
  and a* become derived and their columns are dropped in the 8.4
  revision with DB.73). Boss's refinements of 12:23, 12:24 and 12:25 AM
  EDT, 2026-10-18 (project chat, as the coordinator relayed): any two
  objects that orbit each other follow one rule; before a system is
  validated the heaviest object becomes the primary and the others are
  recalculated from their original values; the barycentre is always the
  origin; coordinates are relative at every level, so a moon follows its
  planet and the planet follows the star; the point-in-space object
  updates the relative coordinates, knows its centre's position in wider
  space and gives converted coordinates for any frame on demand; and it
  also stores the vector of motion, the spin and the other attributes of
  the object with a mass classification. Item SY15 of the note (sections
  12.1 and 13.5). Proposed owner, not assigned by a card: Core 4, with
  GEN.576 and GEN.578. Do: tests that a pair re-primaried gives
  identical absolute positions; the step from the originals is
  idempotent and independent of the order members are listed; `reparent`
  preserves absolute position and velocity; frame round trips (body to
  planet frame to galactic and back) agree to the spacing of a double at
  the top; the mass-weighted offsets sum to zero at every level; a 10 m
  body 10,000 AU from its parent keeps its metre; total linear momentum
  and the orbital angular momentum about the barycentre are unchanged by
  `primary_first` and by `reparent`; a moon's velocity in the star's
  frame equals the sum of its hops; a locked body's rate follows a
  primary change. Do not test that the central object is the closest to
  the barycentre (it is not always: a light member on a tight orbit can
  be nearer); test that it is the heaviest. Done: all pass at several
  depths.
  Prerequisites: GEN.576, GEN.578, GEN.581, GEN.583. Related: GEN.550,
  GEN.565, GEN.576, GEN.578.
  Design: [docs/design/architecture/unified-system-barycentre.md](design/architecture/unified-system-barycentre.md)

  command and CLI path is run end to end (generate, plan, scatter, warm,
  migrate, update.sh, the maintenance timers); the map at every zoom
  level and the System, Sector and Galaxy views are opened at the edges
  of the data (empty sectors, the widest shell, the seam and the black
  hole); the job and queue paths are killed and resumed (stale locks,
  dead tasks, planetgen:run:active); the whole test suite runs with
  `scripts/test.py full --check`, and the flaky and skipped tests are
  listed and explained; the open bugs in docs/TODO.md and the 'could not
  reproduce' list are re-tried on the release candidate; the logs of the
  run are read for warnings and swallowed errors; and a fuzz and
  property pass covers the inputs the tests do not. Done: for the
  release, a dated report
  (/mnt/project-files/reports/release-audit-bug-hunt-<version>.md,
  linked from the goal issue and logged on this item as 'Release log:
  <version>, <EDT date and time>, <commit>') that names the commit
  audited, what was run and what was not, the full-suite result, and
  every bug found filed as its own item with kind, test, failure text,
  whether it fails on main, frequency and reproducer; a bug that breaks
  a headline feature, loses or corrupts data or stops a run blocks the
  release until fixed and merged, the rest are filed with an owner. The
  release is not stamped while the report for its version is missing, or
  while a bug it marks blocking is open. Proposed owner: Bug Hunt (it
  runs the audit; the fixes go to the owning lanes); the 8.1 pass starts
  when the whole-sphere audits merge and the security audit has begun.
  Ordering (TODO thread, 6:40 PM EDT 2026-10-21): this audit runs after
  the performance profile PERF.146 so it sees the final code.
  Owner: a new audit thread, started when PERF.146 closes (Boss, 7:44
  PM EDT 2026-10-22: all five cores on 8.1; this replaces any earlier
  owner line).
  Method: follow /mnt/project-files/reports/audit-playbook-2026-10-22.md
  (the coordinator, relayed 7:58 PM EDT 2026-10-22 as the lane's clock
  reads).
  Gate rule (Boss, 8:04 PM EDT 2026-10-22): the
  version is not stamped while a confirmed Critical or High finding is
  open; Mediums are filed with owners; data loss, corruption or broken
  seed reproducibility counts as High. This holds unless Boss
  specifically authorizes an exception.
  Dead-code pass (Boss, 8:04 PM EDT 2026-10-22): this audit includes
  removing old code that nothing uses any more, in small PRs, one
